$comment: Q7 performance baseline. Every number here is a TRANSCRIPTION of a recording in docs/perf/raw/,
not a judgement about one. `source` names the trace and the exact path inside it;
scripts/perf-budget-guard.test.mjs re-opens each trace and fails the build if this file and the
recording ever disagree. Budgets are derived here and nowhere else -- a budget that appears in a
spec table with no entry in this file also fails the guard.
`budgetKind` separates three things a number in a budget column can mean, because reading them
as one is how a defect gets filed as a spec: `upper bound` = worst recorded + headroom, the app
has earned it; `exact` = budget equals the recording, any drift at all fails; `open finding` =
a ceiling on a KNOWN DEFECT so it cannot grow while the fix is queued, to be re-derived and cut
when the finding closes. An `open finding` row must name the guard or file carrying it.
A row may carry its own `recordedAgainst` when it was re-recorded against a later build than the
file header names -- otherwise one header stamp silently speaks for metrics taken from two
different binaries. The guard validates every override and requires it to differ from the header.
OWED: the traces in docs/perf/raw/ carry no build stamp of their own, so an override is a claim
this file makes about a recording rather than something the recording proves. Stamp them at write
time in scripts/q7-probe.mjs and the guard can check it instead of trusting it.

recordedAgainst.buildStampSource: get_build_stamp over CDP against the installed %LOCALAPPDATA%\Compy\compy.exe
recordedAgainst.machine: Owner desk: AMD Ryzen X3D-class, 16 logical cores ~5.1 GHz, 29.4 GB RAM, Radeon RX 9070 XT (RDNA4), Windows 11 Home 26200, 240 Hz display
recordedAgainst.caveat: ONE rig. Every budget below is an upper bound proven on fast hardware; none of them is a claim about a low-spec target, and the 240 Hz display sets the frame-cadence numbers. A second rig would move these, and Q7's lower-spec leg is still owner-blocked.

coldStartToUsableHomeMs.budgetBasis: Worst recorded start (3721 ms) plus ~20% headroom for a colder disk cache and a busier machine. Set off the WORST sample, never the median: a median budget is one the app fails a third of the time by construction.

coldStartDocumentReadyMs.budgetBasis: NOT AN ACCEPTED COST -- and the CAUSE this row named is now measured, wrong, and retired. Three readings on 2026-08-21 killed every suspect it listed. (1) BUNDLE GROWTH IS RULED OUT: dc4d55e's src/ built with today's toolchain emits index JS 1,536.51 kB + CSS 370.76 kB; HEAD emits 1,538.10 kB + 360.76 kB. The blocking payload is 8.4 kB SMALLER now, and the stylesheet is 2.7% smaller. (2) THE TYPE-1 FONTS ARE RULED OUT: the bundled Geist variable faces (src/design/fonts-v2.css) emit in BOTH builds, byte-identical -- they were already there at 210 ms. (3) THE PAGE ITSELF GOT FASTER: inPageNavigation.domContentLoaded, recorded by the same probe in both traces, reads 103/104/102 ms on dc4d55e and 102/88/87 ms on 584654c8. SO THE ENTIRE GROWTH IS OUTSIDE THE PAGE. This number is clocked from process spawn by a probe that can see nothing until the debug port opens, a CDP session attaches and one evaluate returns, so it silently contains three separate things: spawn -> the page's timeOrigin (Rust init + WebView2 init), the in-page domContentLoaded above, and the probe's own attach lag. None of them was recorded until now. scripts/q7-probe.mjs coldstart records all three from 2026-08-21 (navigationStart / documentReadyInPageMs / observationLag) and they sum EXACTLY to this metric. NOT AN EDGE UPDATE EITHER: the WebView2 runtime is 148.0.3967.83, installed 2026-05-22 and unchanged across both readings. STILL NOT ATTRIBUTED, and do not guess further here -- what is left is the four commits that touched the startup path in that window (git log dc4d55e..HEAD -- src-tauri/src/main.rs src-tauri/src/lib.rs), of which 795d8ff5 (#130) is the one that added startup filesystem work in src-tauri/src/data_root.rs. Settling it needs a decomposed coldstart against a BUILT AND INSTALLED dc4d55e, on a quiet desk. One correction to the previous version of this row: it called the symptom 'a blank window for half a second'. That overstated it. Roughly a fifth of this number is probe attach lag the owner never experiences, and coldStartToUsableHomeMs -- the moment the rail actually appears -- went the OTHER way on the same three starts, 3721 -> 3409 ms worst.

recordedAgainst.why: Re-recorded on 2026-08-21 while answering the owner's "runs a lot slower than before". Its three coldstart siblings still transcribe coldstart.json from dc4d55e and were NOT re-baselined -- only the row that breached moved, so the file does not quietly restate a whole recording to make one number fit.

coldStartWorkingSetMB.statistic: worst of 3, summed across the whole process tree
coldStartWorkingSetMB.budgetBasis: Worst recorded 580 MB across all 8 processes plus ~14%. Deliberately replaces the old 26.50 MB figure in the spec, which counted the compy.exe parent alone and omitted the seven WebView2 processes that hold ~90% of the memory.

coldStartProcessCount.budgetBasis: Exact, not padded. 8 was invariant across three starts (1 compy.exe + 7 WebView2 hosts); a 9th process means a new host or a leaked child, and either is worth failing on rather than absorbing.

bootIpcCallsToFirstPaint.statistic: complete document-start census, first read after mount
bootIpcCallsToFirstPaint.budgetBasis: 29 recorded with a from-document-start instrument, so nothing is missed. Headroom of 5 covers one new panel; it is tight on purpose because 7 of the 29 are duplicate pairs and get_ledger_health alone fires 4x -- the number should be going DOWN, and a budget with room to grow into is a budget that licenses the duplication.

idleIpcCallsPerSecond.statistic: 20 s settle window on Home after boot
idleIpcCallsPerSecond.budgetBasis: Worst of the two Home idle measurements (1.55 here, 1.47 in the room sweep). This is what the app costs while the user reads the screen and does nothing, so it is the figure that compounds over an all-day session.

busiestRoomIpcCallsPerSecond.statistic: 15 s dwell, Monitor -- the busiest of four rooms
busiestRoomIpcCallsPerSecond.budgetBasis: Monitor at 3.0/s is 2x idle Home and is the ceiling across all four rooms: three 1 Hz sensor polls (GPU, CPU, FPS). Budget 4 admits one more 1 Hz sensor and no more; a live monitoring room is allowed to poll, but each poll has to be a deliberate decision.

busiestRoomRafLoops.statistic: rafFired/frames over a 15 s dwell, Monitor
busiestRoomRafLoops.budgetBasis: Derived, not counted by hand: rAF callbacks divided by real frames, with the probe's own tick excluded. Monitor runs ~2 concurrent loops; every other room runs exactly 1. Budget 2.5 fails a third simultaneous loop, which is the shape animation regressions actually take.

keepaliveRoomsIdleIpcPerSecond.statistic: 15 s dwell on Home AFTER all four rooms were mounted and left mounted
keepaliveRoomsIdleIpcPerSecond.budgetBasis: Equal to Home BEFORE any other room existed (1.47, rooms.json#visits.1) -- the keepalive rooms genuinely stand down instead of polling behind display:none. Budget sits just above the recorded value so that any drift toward background polling fails immediately; this is the metric that would catch it.

idleHologramDrawsPerSecond.statistic: 15 s dwell on settled Home, WebGL draw* prototypes counted
idleHologramDrawsPerSecond.budgetBasis: Zero, budgeted at zero. The hologram bay's frameloop="demand" contract says a settled scene must issue no draw calls at all; it spends 240 draws settling and then stops dead. Any nonzero value means the demand loop broke, which is precisely the d557e70 holo-flicker regression.

idleCpuPercentOfOneCore.statistic: consumed processor-seconds over a 10-minute hands-off window, whole process tree, no CDP attached

recordedAgainst.why: Re-recorded after the ambient backdrop stopped animating; the eleven non-idle metrics still describe dc4d55e.

idleCpuPercentOfOneCore.budgetBasis: THE OPEN FINDING IS CLOSED, and this row is an earned bound again. The residual that the 2026-08-19 basis called unsettled has a name: `body::before` drifted forever, and two settled attribution runs on 2026-08-21 measured it at ~88% of everything the app burned sitting idle (22.392% of a core -> 2.067% with that one animation frozen; 21.178 -> 1.681 on the run beside it). Stopping it took the honest whole-app number from 20.853% on 584654c8 to 3.403% here -- same desk, same instrument, same 10-minute hands-off window, no CDP attached. The old 26 was loose enough to hide the entire cost, which is why it is not being left where it was. Budget 4.5 = recorded + 20% rounded up to the next half point, which in practice is +32% -- wider in relative terms than its siblings on purpose: at a number this small the same absolute jitter is a much larger fraction, and the measurement is still ONE rig with window state unproven as a variable (the 2026-08-19 basis named a 2x spread on 3-minute runs that most likely tracked occlusion). What it will no longer do is absorb another always-on animation. The shape rule is held by src/ambient-animation-cost-guard.test.ts guard 6 -- a document-level layer gets a bounded run or none -- and the evidence rule by src/perf-evidence-integrity-guard.test.ts.

idleWorkingSetMB.statistic: max of 20 samples over 10 minutes, whole process tree, fresh boot parked on Home

recordedAgainst.why: Re-recorded with its sibling idle rows after the ambient backdrop stopped animating; the eleven non-idle metrics still describe dc4d55e.

idleWorkingSetMB.budgetBasis: Worst sample of the bare run (568.56 MB) plus ~6%, same derivation as before. The previous basis recorded 605.76 MB and called the +30 MB over the pre-fix 575.16 the price of the 2026-08-06 trade -- work moved off the CPU and onto a retained compositor layer. Stopping the animation drops `will-change: transform` with it, the promoted full-window texture goes away, and the number lands at 568.56 MB: the 30 MB came back and then some. Same statistic, same fresh-boot-parked-on-Home state, same 10-minute window, so those two runs are comparable; a run taken after a room sweep is not. The 570.65 -> 601.35 MB in-window drift the last basis flagged and declined to call a leak did not repeat at this size, which is consistent with allocator behaviour around the promoted layer rather than with a leak; it still takes max-at-10/30/60-minutes from one continuous run to settle that question.
idleWorkingSetMB.headroomNote: 34 MB of headroom left against a budget that was set at 640 pre-fix and is deliberately NOT being raised to restore comfort -- if the next change spends the rest of it, that is the signal to look, not to edit this line.

idlePrivateMB.statistic: max of 20 samples over 10 minutes, whole process tree, fresh boot parked on Home

recordedAgainst.why: Re-recorded with its sibling idle rows after the ambient backdrop stopped animating; the eleven non-idle metrics still describe dc4d55e.

idlePrivateMB.budgetBasis: Worst sample (432.18 MB) plus ~5%. The previous basis had to explain a max: private bytes spiked to 535.14 MB just past the settle window and then held within 4 MB of 434 for the remaining nine minutes, so the row kept max and named the transient. This run has no such gap -- max 432.18 against a median of 426.32 MB -- so max and steady state now agree, and the budget is set against a number that is actually the shape of the app at rest. Max stays the statistic because it is the one that catches a leak. A spike returning, or a median that climbs toward the max, means something different and should fail. Recorded beside working set because they answer different questions -- working set includes shared and mapped pages the OS can reclaim, private bytes is what Compy alone is holding and cannot give back.

roomSwitchLatencyWorstMs.statistic: worst first-mount click-to-content across all rooms (Blackbook and Monitor tie)
roomSwitchLatencyWorstMs.budgetBasis: Worst recorded 19 ms for the heaviest room's genuine first mount (measured from a fresh reload, so the 'first' column is not a warm cache). 60 ms is the perceptual floor where a room switch stops feeling instant -- a 3x margin, because this is the number a slower rig will move most.
